parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Write an equation for the process corresponding to the second ionisation energy of calcium. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Some data relating to calcium and oxygen are listed. Select relevant data from this list for your answers to parts (c), (d) and (e).

| process | value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| first ionisation energy of oxygen | +1310 |
| second ionisation energy of oxygen | +3390 |
| first electron affinity of oxygen | -142 |
| second electron affinity of oxygen | +844 |
| enthalpy change for $\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{O}^{2-}\text{(g)}$ | +951 |
| enthalpy change for $\text{Ca(s)} \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(g)} + 2\text{e}^-$ | +1933 |
| lattice energy of $\text{CaO(s)}$ | -3517 |

Oxygen exists as $\text{O}_2$ molecules.

Use the data in this question to calculate a value for the bond energy of the $\text{O=O}$ bond. Show all your working.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Suggest why the first electron affinity of oxygen is negative.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why the second electron affinity of oxygen is positive.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Calculate the enthalpy of formation of calcium oxide, $\text{CaO(s)}$.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
The lattice energy of lithium fluoride, $\text{LiF(s)}$, is $-1022\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Identify the factor that causes the lattice energy of calcium oxide to be more exothermic than that of lithium fluoride. Explain why this factor causes the difference in lattice energies.
